dedupe_keys.name: ais llm joint vessel trajectory prediction anomaly detection and collision risk assessment with a large language model

description: AIS-LLM is a deep learning framework, described in an August 2025 arXiv preprint by Park, Choi and co-authors, that couples ship automatic identification system (AIS) time series with a large language model to perform three maritime traffic tasks at once. Contents: a time-series encoder for AIS sequences, a prompt encoder, a cross-modality alignment module and a multi-task decoder produce trajectory predictions, anomaly detection and collision risk assessment, and the outputs can be combined into text situation briefings. Coverage: tests on two regions, the Port of Piraeus with 1-minute AIS and Danish waters with 10-minute AIS from the Danish Maritime Authority 2019 release for cargo and tanker vessels, forecasting 24 future positions from 18 past observations. Format and access: preprint PDF; no code release was found. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: not peer reviewed on the pages read, and reported gains are over the authors' chosen baselines. Useful for hazard exposure and emergency response models of port approaches that need short-term traffic forecasts and collision risk. It relates to the Danish Maritime Authority AIS data in the catalogue.
